original_question: For last-passage percolation with general weights, can one prove the full 3:2:1 KPZ scaling law, meaning time scale 3, spatial-correlation scale 2, and fluctuation scale 1 in the KPZ normalization?
target_in_paper: Problem 3 (interacting particle systems and KPZ), especially the open statement on page 7: "In particular showing that LPP with general weights has 3 : 2 : 1 scaling, is far from being resolved."
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the specific model named in the paper (last-passage percolation), the right open direction (general weights rather than only exactly solvable cases), and the right notion of "full" KPZ behavior: the 3:2:1 scaling of time : spatial correlations : fluctuations. It also correctly distinguishes this from results that only establish the fluctuation exponent.
missing_details: The paper presents this as an open problem inside Problem 3, not as a formally numbered conjecture or theorem.
In the paper, 3:2:1 is spelled out as time : spatial correlations : fluctuations = t : t^{2/3} : t^{1/3}; making those exponents explicit makes the question stand alone.
The intended task is a rigorous proof of full KPZ scaling for LPP, not merely a proof of t^{1/3} fluctuation behavior.

The nearby context matters: Deift notes that Brownian LPP is the only model for which full 3:2:1 scaling had been rigorously verified at that time, while Corwin-Liu-Wang had proved KPZ universality only for fluctuations for LPP/TASEP with general initial data.

The phrase "general weights" is not formalized further in this paper: no exact class of weight distributions, no i.i.d. hypothesis, no moment assumptions, and no lattice/continuum normalization are specified here.

Ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree restrictions, nilpotency, operator definitions of an algebraic kind, and clauses such as "for all sufficiently large m" are not part of this probabilistic scaling problem and are inapplicable to the paper's formulation.
refined_question: Can one rigorously show that last-passage percolation with general weights belongs to the KPZ universality class in the full 3:2:1 sense—namely, that on scale t the spatial-correlation length is of order t^{2/3} and the centered last-passage-time fluctuations are of order t^{1/3}—rather than only establishing the fluctuation exponent?
justification: This is the closest paper-faithful sharpening of your draft because Deift first defines KPZ 3:2:1 scaling as time : spatial correlations : fluctuations = t : t^{2/3} : t^{1/3}, then reviews what is known for LPP, and finally singles out the unresolved point that proving 3:2:1 scaling for LPP with general weights remains far from resolved. The refined version therefore stays with LPP itself, keeps the focus on the full 3:2:1 scaling law, and avoids broadening the problem to the KPZ equation more generally or to identification of a specific limiting process, which would go beyond the exact LPP sentence your draft is targeting.

citations.label: Brownian LPP as the only rigorously verified full 3:2:1 example at the time; fluctuations-only result for general initial data
open problem that LPP with general weights has 3:2:1 scaling
